reasoning: The premise that the uncounted generation now practises both kinds of return rests on E8, which is marked hypothetical; the present tense reads that element as an achieved event. E4 says only that the inheritance splits within one generation, not that a whole generation is uncounted. The modal 'may claim standing' is carried by E8, which also says Book 24 names no granting body. The labour-meaning change is not in the cited items.
quote: The cohort, now practising both counted and uncounted return, may claim standing in how the valley coordinates its channel work.
alternative_reading: The claim offered no quote. Read strictly, E8 says the cohort may claim standing, in an element marked hypothetical, so its 'now practising' is not established as current. E4 gives a split within one generation, with unknown_legacy provenance, rather than a wholly uncounted generation.
would_settle: A cited item stating, without a hypothetical marker, that the cohort now practises both returns, and a source naming who grants channel standing.
creative_room: Open: the split may give the valley a new claimant in channel coordination, which a later Book could dramatise as contested without a granting body. Keep current practice, the standing grant and the labour-meaning change as proposals, not record, until a current-status item or granting body exists.

clauses.text: The earlier condition is carried by the cited items.
clauses.note: E4 states the split into counted and uncounted practice; its provenance is unknown_legacy, so the source is unattributed.

clauses.text: It changes what the labour means for the lineage.
clauses.note: Not stated in the cited items; E4 and E8 say nothing about what the labour means to the lineage. Treat as a proposal, not record.

clauses.text: The uncounted generation practises both kinds of return
clauses.note: E8 says 'the cohort, now practising both', in an element marked hypothetical; E4 speaks of a split within one generation, not an uncounted generation.

clauses.text: may, in time, claim standing in channel coordination
clauses.note: E8 carries 'may claim standing' in channel work; 'in time' is not in E8, and E8 says no body grants the standing.

defensible_possibility: That the cohort could, in a later Book, claim standing in channel coordination if it practises both returns; the modal link is in E8 itself and the record names no granting body.
